run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T15:10:25Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend is explained by a short, total outage of the ad service that began right after an ad + payment rollout restart at 15:08:51. The new ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665 carry kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T15:08:51Z (deployment revision 2). Neither deployment defines a readinessProbe, so the new pods were treated as Ready as soon as their containers started (15:08:53-54) and the old pods were scaled down 1-3 seconds later (15:08:54-55). The old ad pod served until about 15:10:25, then ad server-side oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span volume was exactly 0 for every 2-minute window from 15:11:25 through 15:18:25, resuming at 96 at 15:19:25; the new ad pod only logged 'Ad service starting.' at 15:13:18 and served its first ad request at 15:17:47. During that gap frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds failed with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 'UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080' (100.65.180.246 = ClusterIP of Service ad), so frontend's GET /api/data returned HTTP 500. The same restart hit payment: payment server-side Charge spans were 0 in the windows evaluated 15:11:25 and 15:12:25, and checkout's client Charge spans failed with '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card ... dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused' (100.70.188.60 = ClusterIP of Service payment), producing frontend POST /api/checkout 500s. frontend error spans ran from the 15:10:25 minute bucket to the 15:17:25 bucket and were zero before 15:10:25 and from 15:18:25; the all-span error share on frontend was 8.63% at 15:15:00. frontend itself was not restarted (ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5 from 14:35:08) and its /api/cart and /api/products operations recorded no error spans. frontend-proxy recorded matching 500s (about 454 error ingress spans, about 430 error router-frontend-egress spans), and checkout recorded 69.7 error spans, all on PlaceOrder/Charge. Node-level and flagd causes were considered and rejected.

claims.text: In the 14:10:25-15:26:30 window frontend produced about 1734.5 error-status spans (increase): roughly 387 each on GET, GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds; roughly 42.7 each on POST, POST /api/checkout, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder; plus 15.2 on client span tcp.connect. The /api/cart and /api/products paths show 0 error spans.

Exact error detail on frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds: rpc.grpc.status_code=14 with message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080'. Its parent frontend span 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and frontend GET /api/data carry http.status_code 500 / otel.status_code ERROR in the same trace.

100.65.180.246:8080 is the ClusterIP and port of Service ad in namespace otel-demo (selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad, endpoints 100.96.4.142:8080); 100.70.188.60:8080 is the ClusterIP of Service payment (endpoint 100.96.4.221:8080).

The ad service stopped serving completely: ad's server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) counted 49-90 per 2-minute window up to the window evaluated 15:10:25, was 0 for every window evaluated 15:11:25, 15:12:25, 15:13:25, 15:14:25, 15:15:25, 15:16:25, 15:17:25 and 15:18:25, and resumed at 96 at 15:19:25. Frontend's client GetAds error spans mirror it: 0 up to 15:09:25, 16 at 15:10:25, ~51-102 per minute for 15:11:25-15:17:25, then 0 from 15:18:25.

Kubernetes events show the ad and payment workloads were rolled at 15:08:51-55: ReplicaSet ad-6cb57f76d scaled 0->1 and payment-9c8ffb665 scaled 0->1 at 15:08:51, new pods ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 scheduled at 15:08:51 with containers created/started 15:08:53-54, old pods ad-554b849958-mbnxm and payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb killed and deleted at 15:08:54-55, and old ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and payment-55766d76b9 scaled 1->0.

The replacement ReplicaSets are a config-only rollout restart: ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665 have pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T15:08:51Z and deployment revision 2, while ad-554b849958 and payment-55766d76b9 are revision 1 without that annotation; image, env, ports and resources are otherwise unchanged (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and :2.1.3-payment).

Neither the old nor the new ad and payment pod templates define a readinessProbe or a livenessProbe; terminationGracePeriodSeconds is 30, and ad's container resources are limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi with requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi.

The new ad pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 was slow to become usable: the only log line it emitted between 15:08:30 and 15:14:00 is 'Ad service starting.' at 15:13:18, and its first served request ('Targeted ad request received for [books]') is timestamped 15:17:47. Its container reported 0 restarts and no previous container instance.

The payment path failed in the same way and window: checkout's client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge recorded 41.3 error spans in the 2-minute window evaluated 15:11:25 and 2.96 at 15:12:25, while payment's server span grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge was 0 in those two windows (30.7 just before, 74 after). Frontend's span grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder errored with rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and 'failed to charge card ... dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused'. The payment pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 first logged 'Charge request received.' at 15:13:30.

At 15:15:00 the share of error-status frontend spans over all frontend spans was 8.63% (100 * sum(rate(error spans[5m])) / sum(rate(all spans[5m]))). This is the span-based error share I could measure; the alert payload's annotated value is 2.5777 but the rule itself could not be read.

frontend-proxy shows the same failures from its own spans: about 454 error 'ingress' server spans and about 429.8 error 'router frontend egress' client spans in the window, and one trace shows frontend-proxy ingress and egress spans carrying error=true / http.status_code 500 around the frontend GET /api/data 500.

At query time all 21 pods in otel-demo were Running with 0 restarts, and the frontend ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5 was created 2026-11-16T14:35:08Z (ready/available 1, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend) - the frontend was not part of the 15:08:51 rollout.

Among the other services, error-status span series returned 0 for accounting ('orders receive') and cart (flagd EventStream); fraud-detection returned 3.05 and recommendation 4.06 error spans, all on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream reconnects, and those reconnect errors occur intermittently at roughly one per 5 minutes both before and after the 15:10-15:18 burst.

The rollout restart removed the only thing that would have gated traffic: because ad and payment define no readinessProbe, the new pods were Ready as soon as their containers started (old pods scaled 1->0 at 15:08:54/55, 1-3 s after the new containers started at 15:08:53/54), so Service endpoints pointed at pods whose applications had not yet bound port 8080. Connections to the ad and payment ClusterIPs were therefore refused until the new processes actually listened (payment ~15:13, ad 15:17:47).

Ad's very small CPU allowance (limit 50m, request 10m) plausibly stretched its JVM bootstrap - the container started at 15:08:53 but printed 'Ad service starting.' only at 15:13:18 and served its first request at 15:17:47 - which is why ad's outage (~7 minutes) was much longer than payment's (~2 minutes). CPU throttling data was not available to confirm this.

Rejected: a node-level fault on i-0e9f8b08cc290a884, where both the ad and payment pods run. Many other pods share that node (product-catalog, flagd, otel-collector, kafka, currency, email, postgresql, and others), and frontend's calls to product-catalog, recommendation and cart showed no error spans during the burst, so the failure was not node-wide.

Rejected: a frontend application defect or frontend restart as the cause. The frontend pod ran with 0 restarts and its ReplicaSet dates from 14:35:08, and only the operations that call ad (GET /api/data) and checkout/payment (POST /api/checkout) produced error spans, while /api/cart and /api/products produced none; the 500s carry downstream gRPC status 14/13 error messages.

Rejected: the flagd restart as the cause of this alert. A new flagd ReplicaSet flagd-56d9c6c679 appeared at 14:36:48, about 33 minutes before the failure burst, and the only flagd-related errors are scattered EventStream reconnect spans at roughly one per 5 minutes across ad, cart, fraud-detection and recommendation both before and after the incident, with no temporal tie to the 15:10-15:18 errors.

Add a real readinessProbe (gRPC health or TCP 8080) to the ad and payment Deployments - and any other otel-demo Deployment without one - and use a RollingUpdate strategy with maxUnavailable: 0 so the old pod is removed only after the new one actually serves traffic.
Raise ad's CPU limit (currently 50m with a 10m request) or run more than one ad replica, so a cold JVM start does not take minutes, and avoid restarting ad and payment simultaneously under load.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data (status no_data, not citable), so the rule's expression and denominator (annotation says current 2.5777) are unknown and cannot be reconciled with the 8.63% all-span error share measured at 15:15:00.

Frontend container logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs on frontend-675fd7b5c5-h8sk5 returned no_data twice (filtered 15:09-15:20 and unfiltered 14:10-15:26, 0 lines each), so the frontend's own log output cannot corroborate the gRPC failures; only trace spans do.
The old ad and payment pods (ad-554b849958-mbnxm, payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb) were deleted, so their logs and any previous-container logs are not available.

Who or what issued the rollout restart is unknown: the change_history integration is not available for this Run, so whether kubectl rollout restart was deliberate cannot be verified beyond the restartedAt annotation.
No error-status span series was returned for product-catalog, shipping, currency, email, quote, kafka, image-provider or load-generator, so their error status is unknown rather than proven zero.

Span-metric samples in these queries began around 14:48-14:52 and the newest data_as_of was about 15:20:25, so behaviour before 14:48 and after 15:20:25 (including the state when the alert opened at 15:10:25 and whether it later cleared) is outside the returned data.

Two trace-log views were returned incomplete/truncated (the frontend trace search slice showed 40 of 224 rows; ad and payment pod-log reads returned only the newest 30-60 of 276-593 lines), so unread rows remain unknown.
CPU throttling metrics were not queried (not among the available metrics), so the explanation that ad's 50m CPU limit slowed JVM startup remains an unverified hypothesis.
next_steps: Inspect the ad and payment Deployment history and the change record around 2026-11-16T15:08:51Z to confirm who issued the rollout restart and whether it was intentional.
Read the RequestErrorRate alerting rule definition in Prometheus to confirm which metric and denominator produce the reported 2.5777 value.
Check container CPU throttling for the ad pod after a restart (e.g. container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds) to verify the slow-JVM-start hypothesis.
Confirm whether the alert has since cleared by querying frontend error spans after 15:20:25, which is beyond the data returned here.
